Senses.PreferredTarget: directly pointing at the human mind
AlternateTargets: pointing straight at the person's mind
Senses.Explanation: (直) = directly/straight, (指) = point, (人心) = the person's mind. One of the four stock phrases the corpus attaches to Bodhidharma's coming from the West, paired with (見性成佛) ('see nature, become Buddha') in 470 of its 624 allowlist hits (190 files) and preceded by (不立文字) ('not setting up words') in 118 (79 files). Attested deployment: (a) the slogan of what Bodhidharma brought -- (達磨西來不立文字)。(直指人心見性成佛) ('Bodhidharma came from the West not setting up words -- directly pointing at the human mind, seeing nature and becoming Buddha'; Dahui, T47n1997); (達磨西來直指人心見性成佛)。(亦復如是) ('Bodhidharma came from the West directly pointing at the human mind, seeing nature and becoming Buddha; and so it is likewise'; Huitang Zuxin, T51n2077); the Blue Cliff Record (碧巖錄) variant carries (單傳心印) ('the single transmission of the mind-seal') alongside it (謂之教外別傳。單傳心印。直指人心。見性成佛 -- 'this is called a separate transmission outside the teachings, the single transmission of the mind-seal, directly pointing at the human mind, seeing nature and becoming Buddha'; T48n2003); (b) a gloss in a master's own words -- Dahui: (達磨西來不立文字語句)。(唯直指人心)。(若論直指)。(只人人本有) ('Bodhidharma came from the West setting up no words or phrases -- only directly pointing at the human mind; as for direct pointing, just what every person inherently has', T47n1997); (c) a test-question -- (如何是直指人心) ('what is directly pointing at the human mind?'; 4 hits / 4 files), with the recorded answers (舌在口裏) ('the tongue is in the mouth'; the follow-up 如何是見性成佛？師曰：金屑雖貴，落眼成翳 -- 'what is seeing nature and becoming Buddha? The master said: gold dust, though precious, once fallen in the eye becomes a cataract', X82n1571) and (腳跟下分明看取) ('look clearly right under your heels'; answering 如何是直指人心、見性成佛之旨 -- 'what is the purport of directly pointing at the human mind, seeing nature and becoming Buddha?', J34nB311). Collocations: (單傳直指) ('single transmission, direct pointing'; 119 hits / 73 files), (直指單傳) ('direct pointing, single transmission'; 95 / 71), (西來直指) ('the direct pointing of the coming from the West'; 42 / 34), (直指之道) ('the way of direct pointing'; 67 / 34), (若論直指) ('as for direct pointing'; 13 / 13). Beyond recorded lines such as Dahui's (只人人本有) ('just what every person inherently has'), the texts leave the phrase without gloss, and so does this entry.
Senses.Note: 624 hits across 216 files of the 462-file allowlist (XML tags/notes/rdg stripped, whitespace collapsed, punctuation retained -- all counts in this entry use this convention; 見性成佛 ('seeing nature, becoming Buddha') counted as following across at most one punctuation mark). Nearly always in the Bodhidharma four-phrase frame (with 'not setting up words' (不立文字) / 'a separate transmission outside the teachings' (教外別傳) / 'seeing nature, becoming Buddha' (見性成佛)); the paired (見性成佛) is its near-constant companion (470 of 624 hits). Curated occurrences span a master's (語錄) ('recorded sayings'; Dahui), a (古尊宿) ('Ancient Worthies') anthology, a (燈錄) ('lamp record'; the 續傳燈錄, Continued Lamp Record), and the (碧巖錄) (the Blue Cliff Record, T48n2003 -- a 頌古/評唱 collection of verse-comments on old cases and prose expositions, a case-commentary collection, not a lamp record).
